encodeFrames.explanation: Encodes an explicit list of PNG images into one silent, constant-frame-rate video (video.mp4 for H.264 or video.mkv for FFV1); each list entry becomes exactly one frame lasting 1/fps seconds. A fresh FFmpeg decode is compared pixel-by-pixel with the source images. Choose it for rendered image sequences (for example ParaView, Blender or Inkscape frames); use encodeSheet for an Aseprite sprite sheet with per-frame durations.
pitfalls: Files are not sorted; list them in playback order. Repeating a path repeats that frame.
All frames must be 8-bit RGB or RGBA, non-interlaced PNGs of identical size; palette, greyscale and 16-bit PNGs are rejected.
H.264 needs even width and height; use FFV1 or re-render at an even size.
Transparent areas are composited onto black, and no audio track is written.

encodeSheet.explanation: Cuts frame rectangles out of one sprite-sheet PNG, using a schemaxis.aseprite.sheet/1 JSON file for their positions and millisecond durations, and encodes them in metadata order into one silent constant-frame-rate video. Each rectangle is repeated for durationMS x fps / 1000 video frames. Choose it for Aseprite animation output; use encodeFrames for separate image files.
pitfalls: Every frame duration must be a whole number of video frames: at 25 fps durations must be multiples of 40 ms, otherwise UNSUPPORTED_TIMING.
Metadata order is playback order; tags in the metadata do not select or reorder frames.
All rectangles must have the same size, and the sheet's pixel size must match the metadata width and height.

fields.explanation: One FFmpeg video publication: a single node that encodes PNG frames or a sprite sheet into a silent video at a constant frame rate, plus optional deliverable requirements. Limits: 600 frames, 4096 pixels per side and 192 MiB of decoded pixels.

/properties/version.explanation: Format identifier of this Schemaxis document; it must be "schemaxis.ffmpeg/1". It is not the FFmpeg release.

/properties/nodes.explanation: Declare exactly one video publication node, choosing an ordered PNG list or a timed sprite sheet.

/properties/nodes/items.explanation: The single publication node describes the source images, frame rate, codec and encoder resources.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0.explanation: Encode an ordered list of equally sized PNG frames; each list entry becomes one video frame. Choose this for rendered image sequences, and the sprite-sheet alternative for Aseprite sheets with frame durations.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Name of this video publication, used in logs and when other workflow steps refer to its result. Start with a letter; then use letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.
encodeFrames: encode a list of separate PNG files, one video frame per entry. Switch to encodeSheet for a sprite sheet with frame durations.

Frame list and encoding settings. files (required) sets the content and order; fps, codec and threads keep their defaults (25, h264, 1) when omitted. The codec choice decides whether the video is lossless.
Constant video frame rate, an integer from 1 to 120 frames per second. Each listed file is shown for exactly 1/fps seconds, so the video lasts (number of files) / fps seconds.

Choose H.264 MP4 for compact lossy YUV420 video or FFV1 Matroska for byte-exact RGB after alpha compositing. Default H.264 requires even dimensions; every frame must remain within the 16-level mean RGB error bound.
Native encoder/decoder thread count, 1 to 16; default 1. Workflow allocation must match this setting; it does not enable MPI.
Absolute paths of 1 to 600 PNG images in playback order, or workflow references to image artifacts. Repeating a path repeats that frame; no filename sorting or wildcard expansion is done.
pitfalls: Every image must be an 8-bit RGB or RGBA, non-interlaced PNG of the same size (each file at most 32 MiB).
Relative paths are rejected during planning.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: An absolute PNG path in playback order. The retained source bytes allow offline verification after the original input disappears.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1.explanation: Encode an animation stored as one sprite-sheet PNG plus its schemaxis.aseprite.sheet/1 metadata: rectangles are extracted in metadata order and each is held for its declared duration. Choose this for Aseprite output; use the frame-list alternative for separate PNG files.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: Name of this video publication, used in logs and when other workflow steps refer to its result. Start with a letter; then use letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.
encodeSheet: encode rectangles from one sprite-sheet PNG using its timing metadata. Switch to encodeFrames for a list of separate PNG files.
Sprite-sheet source and encoding settings. file and metadata are required; fps, codec and threads keep their defaults (25, h264, 1) when omitted. fps must divide every frame duration exactly.
Constant video frame rate in frames per second, an integer from 1 to 120; default 25. A sheet duration must be an exact multiple of one video frame period.

Choose H.264 MP4 for compact lossy YUV420 video or FFV1 Matroska for byte-exact RGB after alpha compositing. Default H.264 requires even dimensions; every frame must remain within the 16-level mean RGB error bound.
Native encoder/decoder thread count, 1 to 16; default 1. Workflow allocation must match this setting; it does not enable MPI.
Absolute path of the sprite-sheet PNG (8-bit RGB or RGBA, non-interlaced, at most 32 MiB). Its pixel width and height must equal the width and height recorded in the metadata file.

Absolute path of the schemaxis.aseprite.sheet/1 JSON written by the Aseprite adaptor, listing 1 to 600 frame rectangles (x, y, width, height in pixels) and durations in milliseconds. Frame order is playback order; tags do not select or reorder frames.
pitfalls: Each durationMS x fps must be a multiple of 1000 (for example 40 ms steps at 25 fps); otherwise UNSUPPORTED_TIMING.
All rectangles must have the same size and lie inside the sheet.

/properties/deliverable.explanation: Declare at least one media requirement. Verification measures the result and rejects unmet requirements with an explained corrective action; no automatic scaling or encoder search is performed.

/properties/deliverable/properties/width.explanation: Required output width in pixels, 1 to 4096. Sources must already have this width; this requirement does not resize them.

/properties/deliverable/properties/heigh.explanation: Required output height in pixels, 1 to 4096. Sources must already have this height; this requirement does not resize them.

/properties/deliverable/properties/frame.explanation: Required exact number of encoded frames, 1 to 600. Sprite durations can repeat source rectangles over several video frames.

/properties/deliverable/properties/durat.explanation: Target native video duration in seconds, from 1/120 to 600. Compare the observed container duration with this target using the absolute tolerance.
Absolute allowed duration difference in seconds, 0 to 1; default 0.002. Supply a duration target when specifying a tolerance. Container time precision may prevent a zero-tolerance target.

/properties/deliverable/properties/maxBy.explanation: Maximum encoded file size in bytes, 1 to 1073741824. A correct video exceeding the budget is retained with an unmet assessment; choose a different codec or reduce source dimensions/frame count.

/properties/deliverable/properties/maxMe.explanation: Maximum per-frame mean absolute RGB byte error, 0 to 16. Zero requires exact composited RGB; FFV1 always requires exactness independently. This is a pixel-error budget, not perceptual quality certification.
